newsitem.title: CHINA: China says calm returns to riot-hit Moslem town.
newsitem.headline: China says calm returns to riot-hit Moslem town.

text.p: Calm has returned to a town hit by ethnic unrest this month in China's mainly Moslem northwestern region of Xinjiang, a Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesman said on Tuesday.

"At present, calm has returned there," ministry spokesman Tang Guoqiang told a news briefing in reference to the town of Yining, where nine people were killed and 198 injured in rioting on February 5-6.

Chinese police arrested up to 300 people after the anti-Chinese riot in Xinjiang, which Moslem separatists call East Turkestan, local officials said. Many had been released after interrogation, they said.

About 1,000 people, mostly Uighur farmers or unemployed young men, took part in the demonstration for independence, one of the largest and most violent in Xinjiang since the communist takeover in 1949.
Yining is 50 km (30 miles) from the border with Kazakhstan, where many exiled Uighur separatists live.
"A small group of thugs incited people to break the law and engaged in beating people, smashing, pillaging and other criminal activities," Tang said.
"These activities disrupted social order... Local law enforcement organisations adopted measures in accordance with the law to prevent and stop criminal activities," he said.
"It was to protect the property of the state and the lives and safety of the people," the spokesman said.
Local officials said suspected ringleader Abudu Heilili had been arrested.

Xinjiang, bordering Afghanistan, Pakistan and three mostly Moslem Central Asian states, was shaken last year by bombings and assassination attempts on officials and Moslem leaders regarded as pro-Beijing.

Yusupbek Mukhlisi, leader of the United National Revolutionary Front of East Turkestan based in Kazakhstan, said the riot was sparked by the execution of 30 Uighurs in China this month. Chinese officials dismissed the allegation.
Turkic-speaking Uighurs are in the majority in Xinjiang, where ethnic Han Chinese make up 38 percent of the population.
